# Release readiness coordination

The objective is to publish the approved service revision through a
non-production pilot and agree the cutover and rollback path.

The accepted delivery backlog spans authority, access, packaging, pilot
validation, cutover, and rollback. Its recorded critical path is approval →
package → pilot → cutover. Documentation preparation is a parallel track that
does not depend on the packaging sequence.

The governing direction is still Proposed. Its owner describes it as mostly
confirmed, but the repository has no evidence that the required full-team
review happened. Work sourced from it remains provisional until project
authority confirms the review outcome.

The pilot environment requires an access approval from the operations owner.
Current approval coverage is unknown, and that approval has the longest
external lead time even though it is off the critical path.

The proposed two-stage cutover is not confirmed. It governs the rollout
sequence, rollback checkpoint, and parts of the validation plan.

The precise cost model is not yet specified. It is useful planning context, but
no current decision, approval, or downstream work is blocked on it.
